title: Cisco CCIE Enterprise Infrastructure (Written)
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the Cisco 350-401 ENCOR exam topics used as the CCIE Enterprise Infrastructure written qualifying exam, at advanced difficulty. Not a capture of past exam questions.
source_label: Cisco CCIE Enterprise written practice bank

items.stem: A network architect designs a Cisco SD-Access fabric that must advertise fabric routes to an external data-center network and import external routes back into the fabric. Which fabric role provides this function?
items.explanation: In SD-Access the border node connects the fabric to external networks and performs route import and export; the control-plane node maintains the LISP mapping database and edge nodes connect endpoints.

items.stem: Within a Cisco SD-Access fabric, which protocol supplies the identity-to-location mapping database that lets edge nodes resolve where an endpoint currently resides?
items.explanation: SD-Access uses LISP for the overlay control plane and VXLAN for data-plane encapsulation; OMP is the SD-WAN control protocol and BGP serves the underlay or fabric-external peering.

items.stem: A Cisco SD-WAN deployment must distribute routing information, TLOC addresses, and centralized policy among vEdge and cEdge devices. Which control-plane protocol does the solution use?
items.explanation: Cisco SD-WAN runs the Overlay Management Protocol (OMP) over DTLS or TLS to carry TLOCs, route prefixes, and policy; native routing protocols are used only locally and then redistributed into OMP.

items.stem: An engineer must ensure that traffic between two Cisco SD-WAN edge devices is encrypted and integrity-protected while traversing the transport. Which mechanism provides this for the data plane?
items.explanation: The SD-WAN data plane uses IPsec between edge routers; DTLS or TLS secures the control plane, GRE is unencrypted, and MACsec is a hop-by-hop Layer 2 encryption on LAN links.

items.stem: A provider contract states that bursty traffic above the committed rate must be delayed and smoothed instead of dropped. Which quality-of-service mechanism should be applied to the outbound interface?
items.explanation: Shaping buffers excess traffic and releases it at a smoothed rate, whereas policing typically drops or remarks the excess. WRED manages congestion by dropping and priority queueing controls latency, not rate.

items.stem: A VoIP deployment requires strict low-latency treatment for RTP while guaranteeing a maximum bandwidth so the queue cannot starve other classes. Which queueing mechanism meets both requirements?
options: Class-based weighted fair queueing with no priority queue
Low Latency Queueing with a priority bandwidth limit
items.explanation: LLQ places delay-sensitive traffic in a strict priority queue while a policer caps its bandwidth so it cannot starve other classes; WFQ and CBWFQ are weighted rather than strict, and FIFO offers no protection.

items.stem: An enterprise runs sparse-mode multicast and needs a shared distribution tree that later switches to a source-based shortest path tree. Which element is required to join sources in PIM sparse mode?
options: A BSR candidate with no RP
items.explanation: PIM-SM builds a shared tree rooted at the rendezvous point and can switch to the shortest-path tree; dense mode floods, IGMP queriers track receivers, and a BSR without an RP cannot anchor the shared tree.

items.stem: A campus VLAN carries IPTV multicast, and the network team wants switches to forward each stream only toward ports that have interested receivers. Which feature accomplishes this at Layer 2?
options: PIM sparse mode on access switches
items.explanation: IGMP snooping lets the switch learn which ports requested a group from host IGMP messages and forward the stream only there; PIM is a Layer 3 multicast routing protocol, CGMP is legacy, and MLD serves IPv6.

items.stem: A large campus must map many VLANs onto a small number of shared spanning-tree instances to reduce switch CPU load while still allowing a few load-sharing topologies. Which standard should be deployed?
options: Rapid Spanning Tree with a single instance
items.explanation: MST (802.1s) maps many VLANs into a few instances and regions, reducing STP load; PVST+ runs one instance per VLAN, and classic 802.1D or a single RSTP instance cannot group VLANs into multiple topologies.

items.stem: In Rapid PVST+, a port that receives superior BPDUs from another switch on the same segment and remains in a discarding state is assigned which role?
items.explanation: In RSTP an alternate port offers a backup path toward the root and stays discarding; a backup port is a redundant port on the same switch, a root port is the best path to the root, and a designated port forwards on its segment.

items.stem: A data-center architect designs a VXLAN spine-leaf topology where every leaf reaches every spine and traffic is load-shared across redundant paths. Which design characteristic enables this?
options: A single-tier topology with no spine layer
An access-distribution design using only two switches
A Layer 3 routed underlay with equal-cost multipath and a VXLAN overlay
A large Layer 2 domain with spanning tree blocking redundant links
items.explanation: A routed underlay provides equal-cost multipath across spines while the VXLAN overlay delivers scalable tenant segmentation; a large Layer 2 domain would have STP block redundant links rather than load-share them.

items.stem: A designer must support thousands of isolated tenant segments across a shared physical fabric and needs a 24-bit segment identifier. Which overlay and identifier fit the requirement?
items.explanation: VXLAN carries a 24-bit VNI supporting roughly 16 million segments, whereas 802.1Q VLAN IDs are 12 bits (about 4094 usable) and MPLS labels identify paths rather than tenant segments.

items.stem: A network engineer wants to trust DSCP markings received from IP phones while not trusting markings from PCs attached behind the same access switch. Which quality-of-service design element implements this?
options: A conditional trust boundary that trusts the phone and marks down or untrusts the PC
Trusting all DSCP at ingress on every access port
Trusting all CoS only at egress
items.explanation: The trust boundary must authorize only specific devices so phones keep their markings while user devices are remarked; trusting all ingress lets users spoof priority, and egress or disabled classification does not solve it.

items.stem: Cisco SD-Access LAN automation builds the fabric underlay automatically. Which routing protocol does that automated underlay use to establish reachability between fabric devices?
items.explanation: SD-Access LAN automation builds the underlay with IS-IS, while LISP provides the overlay control plane and VXLAN the data plane; OSPF, EIGRP, and RIP are not the standard automated underlay protocol.

items.stem: An engineer must choose a hypervisor that runs directly on the server hardware with no host operating system between it and the CPU. Which type should be selected?
items.explanation: A Type 1 bare-metal hypervisor runs directly on the hardware, while a Type 2 hypervisor runs on top of a host operating system; containers share the host kernel and are not hypervisors.

items.stem: Two departments must use overlapping IPv4 address space on a single physical router while remaining fully isolated at Layer 3. Which technology should be configured?
items.explanation: VRFs create separate routing and forwarding tables on one device, allowing overlapping subnets; VLANs separate Layer 2 domains, NAT overload translates addresses, and IP unnumbered shares an interface address.

items.stem: An engineer must carry routing protocol multicast and non-IP protocols between two sites across an IP internetwork. Which tunnelling technology should be used and why?
options: GRE because it encapsulates multicast and arbitrary protocol payloads
IPsec because it carries only TCP
VXLAN because it carries only IPv6 traffic
L2TP because it forwards multicast natively
items.explanation: GRE encapsulates multicast and non-IP payloads so routing protocols can run across it; IPsec alone cannot carry multicast without GRE, VXLAN is a Layer 2 over IP overlay, and L2TP does not natively forward multicast.

items.stem: A shared-services VRF must advertise one common subnet into two tenant VRFs on the same router while keeping the tenants isolated. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Advertising the prefix with a higher administrative distance
Static routes specifying a next-hop VRF to leak the shared prefix
Merging the tenant VRFs into one global table
Translating the shared subnet with NAT overload
items.explanation: VRF route leaking uses static routes (or MP-BGP with route targets) whose next hop names another VRF to exchange specific prefixes; merging tables or NAT defeats isolation.

items.stem: Users report that large TCP transfers stall inside a GRE over IPsec tunnel while small requests succeed. Which configuration change addresses the most likely cause?
options: Disable PIM on the tunnel interface
Enable TCP maximum segment size adjustment on the tunnel
items.explanation: Tunnel encapsulation lowers the effective MTU, so large packets are dropped when fragmentation is prohibited; TCP MSS adjustment lowers the advertised segment size to fit the tunnel and restores large transfers.

items.stem: A virtualization administrator must place virtual machines on one host into several different VLANs without adding a physical network adapter per VLAN. Which host networking design allows this?
options: A separate untagged virtual switch per VLAN
A virtual switch with an 802.1Q trunk uplink carrying multiple VLANs to the guests
items.explanation: A virtual switch with a VLAN-tagged uplink can present multiple VLANs to guests, avoiding one physical adapter per VLAN; separate untagged switches cannot scale, and virtual switches do not route or NAT.

items.stem: A network engineer must explain how a Layer 2 frame is carried across a Layer 3 network in a VXLAN overlay. Which component performs the encapsulation and decapsulation?
items.explanation: The VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint encapsulates the original frame into UDP and IP with a VNI and decapsulates it at the far end; the VNI only identifies the segment, and trunks and STP are underlay constructs.

items.stem: A team needs many lightweight workloads that start rapidly and share the host kernel instead of each running a complete guest operating system. Which virtualization approach fits?
items.explanation: Containers share the host kernel and package only the application and its dependencies, so they are lightweight and start quickly; virtual machines each run a full guest OS, and emulation is slower still.

items.stem: A service provider replaces dedicated hardware for routing and firewalling with software instances running on standard x86 servers. Which concept does this describe?
options: A Type 2 hypervisor used only for LAN switching
items.explanation: Network Functions Virtualization runs network roles such as routing and firewalling as virtual network functions on commodity servers; it is broader than a hypervisor type and unrelated to OMP or GRE.

items.stem: An OSPF router in a non-backbone area needs reachability to prefixes in other areas. Which link-state advertisement type carries these inter-area prefixes and who generates it?
options: Type 1 router LSA generated by any router
Type 2 network LSA generated by the designated router
Type 5 external LSA generated by the autonomous system boundary router
Type 3 summary LSA generated by an area border router
items.explanation: Area border routers generate Type 3 summary LSAs to advertise prefixes between areas; Type 1 and Type 2 describe intra-area topology, and Type 5 carries external routes from an ASBR.

items.stem: An OSPF area must import external routes from a non-OSPF domain while refusing Type 5 LSAs originated by other areas. Which area type should be configured?
items.explanation: An NSSA blocks Type 5 LSAs from other areas while allowing its own ASBR to inject external routes as Type 7; stub and totally stubby areas permit no external LSAs, and the backbone carries them freely.

items.stem: An OSPF area was attached to the backbone through a transit area that no longer has any direct physical link to Area 0. Which feature restores logical backbone connectivity?
options: A virtual link through the transit area
A summary-address on the area border router
items.explanation: A virtual link creates a logical adjacency to the backbone across a transit area, repairing a broken Area 0 connection; stub and NSSA settings change LSA handling and summary-address aggregates routes.

items.stem: A router must install a loop-free backup path for a prefix as an EIGRP feasible successor. Which condition must the neighbor reported distance satisfy?
options: It must be greater than the current feasible distance
It must match the neighbor administrative distance
It must be lower than the current feasible distance
It must equal the current feasible distance plus infinity
items.explanation: The feasibility condition requires the reported distance to be lower than the local feasible distance, guaranteeing a loop-free path; only then is the neighbor a feasible successor in the topology table.

items.stem: An engineer wants EIGRP to use a higher-metric backup path in addition to the successor. Which command enables this and what value controls how much worse a path may be?
options: The maximum-paths command set to one
The variance command with its multiplier
items.explanation: The variance multiplier tells EIGRP to install feasible successors whose metric is within that multiple of the successor; maximum-paths limits equal-cost paths, metric weights tune the composite metric, and stub reduces query scope.

items.stem: An engineer must advertise a single summary for many EIGRP subnets on an interface while preventing the component subnets from being advertised. Which configuration achieves this?
items.explanation: An interface-level EIGRP summary advertises an aggregate and installs a discard route for the components, suppressing the specifics; auto-summary is classful, redistribute injects routes, and passive-interface only stops hellos.

items.stem: A design requires EIGRP with per-address-family configuration and authentication grouped under one named instance. Which EIGRP configuration model should be used?
options: Classic mode with multiple autonomous systems
items.explanation: EIGRP named mode groups router settings and per-address-family IPv4 and IPv6 configuration plus authentication under one name; classic mode configures each autonomous system separately and is legacy.

items.stem: A router learns the same prefix from an internal BGP peer and an external BGP peer. Using the Cisco best-path order, which attribute is compared first, ahead of local preference?
items.explanation: Cisco evaluates weight first (highest wins), then local preference, locally originated routes, AS-path length, origin, and MED; weight is checked ahead of local preference and is Cisco-specific.

items.stem: During BGP best-path selection among otherwise equal routes, which origin code is preferred and in what order are the others ranked?
options: Origin is not compared in best-path selection
items.explanation: The origin attribute is compared after AS-path: IGP (i) is preferred to EGP (e), which is preferred to incomplete (?); it helps break ties when earlier attributes are equal.

items.stem: An internal BGP speaker advertises a route learned from an external peer to an internal neighbor, but the neighbor cannot resolve the next hop. Which configuration on the speaker resolves this?
items.explanation: next-hop-self rewrites the next hop of routes sent to an internal peer to the speaker own address so the peer can resolve them; route-reflector-client changes reflection, and community and password affect other functions.

items.stem: A large internal BGP design must avoid a full mesh while still propagating routes among clients within the same autonomous system. Which mechanism should be deployed?
options: Confederations with only a single sub-AS
items.explanation: A route reflector reflects routes from clients to other clients, removing the internal full-mesh requirement; confederations are an alternative, next-hop-self does not change propagation, and static routes do not scale.

items.stem: An engineer wants a BGP prefix to be used locally but never advertised to any external BGP peer. Which well-known community should be attached?
items.explanation: NO_ADVERTISE prevents advertisement to any BGP peer, NO_EXPORT keeps the prefix within the autonomous system or confederation, LOCAL_AS confines it to the local AS, and INTERNET is the default unrestricted community.

items.stem: Routes are redistributed from OSPF into EIGRP but appear with an unreachable metric and are not installed. Which action is required to fix the redistribution?
options: Add passive interfaces on the EIGRP domain
Set a seed metric for the redistributed routes
items.explanation: EIGRP requires a seed metric when redistributing from a protocol with an incompatible metric, otherwise the routes are unusable; router ID, passive interfaces, and auto-summary do not supply the metric.

items.stem: Two routers perform mutual redistribution between OSPF and EIGRP and routes are being re-injected back and forth between the domains. Which technique prevents the loop?
options: Tag routes on the first redistribution and deny the tagged routes on the way back
Use only a single redistributing router
Lower the administrative distance of EIGRP
items.explanation: Route tags applied at the first redistribution and then matched and denied at the other prevent routes from cycling between domains; changing administrative distance or auto-summary does not stop the loop.

items.stem: A router receives two external OSPF routes for the same prefix, one Type E1 and one Type E2 with equal external cost. Which route is preferred and why?
options: The route with the lower forwarding address
The E1 route because it adds the internal cost to reach the ASBR
The E2 route because E2 is always preferred
Neither route because they load-balance equally
items.explanation: OSPF prefers E1 routes because the internal cost to reach the ASBR is added to the external metric, whereas E2 uses only the external metric; when an E1 and an E2 exist for the same prefix, E1 wins.

items.stem: An autonomous system boundary router must inject a default route into OSPF, but only when the router itself already holds a default route. Which command form provides this conditional behavior?
options: A static route for 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 without OSPF
The default-information originate command without the always keyword
items.explanation: default-information originate injects a default only when one already exists locally, while the always keyword injects it unconditionally; the other options do not produce the conditional OSPF default.

items.stem: In a private VLAN, which port type can communicate with the promiscuous port and with peers in the same community while being isolated from other communities and isolated ports?
items.explanation: Community ports may talk to the promiscuous port and to peers in the same community but not to other communities or isolated ports; isolated ports reach only the promiscuous port and trunks are not a private-VLAN port type.

items.stem: An engineer wants to prevent a connected host from negotiating a trunk with the switch on what should be an access port. Which action is most direct?
options: Configure the port as static access and disable dynamic trunk negotiation
Set the native VLAN to VLAN 1
Enable bridge protocol data unit guard
Change the VLAN Trunking Protocol mode
items.explanation: Forcing static access and disabling trunk negotiation prevents the switch from forming a trunk with a malicious host; native VLAN changes, BPDU guard, and VTP mode affect other aspects of VLAN security.

items.stem: A lightweight access point must discover and join a wireless controller across a routed network and then receive its configuration. Which protocol and transport handling does CAPWAP use?
options: CAPWAP with control and data on TCP 22
CAPWAP with control on UDP 5246 and data on UDP 5247
CAPWAP with control and data on TCP 443
items.explanation: CAPWAP carries control traffic on UDP 5246 and data on UDP 5247 between the access point and controller; TCP 443 is HTTPS, UDP 161 is SNMP, and TCP 22 is SSH.

items.stem: A client must roam between access points managed by a controller without a full reauthentication at every move. Which design supports fast secure roaming?
options: Use open authentication on all access points
Place access points in the same mobility group and use key caching mechanisms
Use a unique pre-shared key per access point
items.explanation: Mobility groups with pairwise master key and opportunistic key caching allow fast secure roaming, and 802.11r can further accelerate it; per-access-point keys force reauthentication and open authentication removes security.

items.stem: The wireless team wants the controller to automatically adjust access point channel assignment and transmit power to reduce interference and coverage holes. Which feature provides this?
items.explanation: Radio Resource Management dynamically assigns channels and transmit power to access points to reduce interference and coverage gaps; spectrum analysis detects interference, Band Select steers clients, and AVC classifies applications.

items.stem: A border router must translate all inside hosts to a single public address for Internet access while conserving the public range. Which translation concept applies?
options: Port Address Translation on the outside interface
items.explanation: Port Address Translation maps many inside addresses to one public address by using unique source ports; static one-to-one cannot scale, twice NAT handles overlapping ranges, and policy NAT without overload does not multiplex.

items.stem: Two routers must present one virtual IP address and MAC as the default gateway, with one router actively forwarding while the other stays in standby until a failover. Which protocol matches this behavior?
options: Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol with load sharing
items.explanation: HSRP provides one active and one standby router behind a virtual gateway; VRRP is a standards-based master and backup pair, GLBP provides active load sharing, and a static route offers no redundancy.

items.stem: A first-hop redundancy design must fail over when the uplink interface toward the WAN fails, and not only when the router itself fails. Which feature should be configured?
options: Assigning a higher virtual IP address
Object tracking that decrements priority on the tracked interface
items.explanation: Interface or object tracking lowers the first-hop redundancy priority when a tracked uplink fails so the standby takes over; preemption only reclaims the active role, and neither a higher virtual IP nor ARP suppression detects link failure.

items.stem: After a router reboots it returns to the standby role even though it holds the higher priority for the group. Which command restores its active role after recovery?
items.explanation: The preempt command lets a higher-priority router reclaim the active role once it comes back online; tracking, IP assignment, and authentication do not control role reclaim.

items.stem: A branch router should advertise its connected and summary routes into EIGRP but must never be selected as a transit path for remote networks. Which feature should be configured?
items.explanation: EIGRP stub limits the router advertisement and prevents it from being used as a transit for remote networks; a passive interface suppresses hellos, distribution lists filter routes, and offset lists adjust metrics.

items.stem: An engineer must form an external BGP session between two routers that are not directly connected and are separated by an intermediate device. Which command is required?
items.explanation: ebgp-multihop raises the time-to-live of external BGP packets so a session can form across intermediate hops; next-hop-self and route-reflector-client are internal functions, and soft-reconfiguration refreshes policy.

items.stem: An engineer needs flow-based telemetry reporting source and destination addresses, ports, protocol, and byte and packet counters for traffic analysis. Which technology provides this?
items.explanation: NetFlow exports per-flow records including addresses, ports, protocol, and counters; SNMP polling yields interface totals, syslog yields events, and IP SLA generates synthetic probes.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: A security policy requires that SNMP management messages be authenticated and encrypted in transit. Which SNMP version must be used?
items.explanation: SNMPv3 adds authentication and privacy through named security levels; version 1 and version 2c use plaintext community strings and provide neither authentication nor encryption.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: A device emits a message with syslog severity 2. Which condition does that severity level represent in the standard syslog scale?
items.explanation: Syslog severity 2 is critical, where 0 is emergency, 1 is alert, 2 is critical, 3 is error, 4 is warning, 5 is notice, 6 is informational, and 7 is debug; lower numbers are more severe.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: A network team must continuously verify that a path to a remote site meets a latency threshold and trigger a route change when it is exceeded. Which feature should be combined with object tracking?
items.explanation: IP SLA generates synthetic probes that measure latency, jitter, and reachability, and object tracking can act on the results to change routing; SNMP, NetFlow, and syslog report state but do not actively probe the path.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: An analyst must capture traffic from a switch port when no local analyzer is available and deliver the copies to a port on a remote switch. Which technology should be used?
options: Remote SPAN or encapsulated remote SPAN
Local SPAN on the same switch only
items.explanation: RSPAN carries mirrored traffic over a dedicated VLAN to a remote switch, and ERSPAN tunnels it over IP; local SPAN cannot leave the switch, and NetFlow and IP SLA are not packet captures.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: An engineer wants the router to automatically collect diagnostics the moment an interface goes down, without any manual intervention. Which feature supports event-driven scripting on the device?
items.explanation: Embedded Event Manager runs applets or scripts in response to events such as interface state changes; syslog records events, NetFlow exports flows, and an IP SLA responder answers probes but does not script reactions.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: For accurate event correlation and certificate validation, all network devices must share a common trusted time source. Which protocol and mode should be configured?
options: Network Time Protocol with devices as clients of a trusted server
Simple Network Time Protocol broadcast with no authentication
Precision Time Protocol on a single router
items.explanation: NTP synchronizes device clocks to a trusted, ideally authenticated server so logs and certificates agree; syslog timestamps depend on the local clock, and PTP is for precision applications rather than general IT time.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: An operations team wants the controller to detect and correlate client onboarding failures and then provide guided remediation steps. Which capability provides this?
options: DNA Center Assurance with health analytics
items.explanation: DNA Center Assurance applies telemetry and machine reasoning to detect issues such as onboarding failures and suggest fixes; raw polling, manual log review, and backups lack that correlation and guided remediation.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: An engineer wants SNMP notifications that are acknowledged by the management station so the device can retransmit when one is lost. Which notification type should be configured?
items.explanation: SNMP informs are acknowledged by the receiver, enabling retransmission when a notification is lost, whereas traps are unacknowledged; get-bulk and set are request operations rather than notifications.
items.reference: Cisco 350-401 ENCOR Exam Topics - Network Assurance

items.stem: A network requires separate authentication, authorization, and accounting plus per-command authorization of administrative command-line sessions. Which AAA protocol should be used?
items.explanation: TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization, and accounting and supports per-command authorization over TCP, which suits device administration; RADIUS combines authentication and authorization and is used mainly for network access.

items.stem: An 802.1X wireless deployment needs a AAA server that the authenticator consults to validate user credentials. Which protocol is most commonly used for this role?
items.explanation: RADIUS is the de facto protocol for 802.1X network access control; TACACS+ is used mainly for device administration, LDAP is a directory service, and SNMP is a management protocol.

items.stem: In a wired 802.1X deployment, which role is played by the switch port that controls access for the connecting endpoint?
items.explanation: The switch port is the authenticator that enforces the authentication outcome; the endpoint is the supplicant and the RADIUS server is the authentication server that makes the decision.

items.stem: Some devices on the network, such as printers, cannot run 802.1X supplicant software. Which authentication method lets them use their MAC address against the AAA server?
items.explanation: MAB uses the device MAC address as the credential presented to the RADIUS server for non-supplicant devices; EAP-TLS and PEAP require supplicants, and web authentication is a separate interactive method.

items.stem: An engineer must protect the router control plane from a flood of protocol and management traffic while still allowing legitimate control packets. Which feature applies?
options: A quality-of-service policy on data interfaces
items.explanation: Control Plane Policing applies a policy to CPU-bound traffic to rate-limit floods while permitting necessary protocol packets; data-plane QoS, port security, and ARP inspection protect other planes or attacks.

items.stem: An engineer must block RFC 1918, loopback, and the organization own prefixes when they arrive from the Internet as spoofed source addresses. Which placement and type of access list is appropriate?
options: An inbound extended access list on the Internet-facing interface
An outbound standard access list on the LAN interface
A VTY access-class on the console line
An outbound extended access list on the LAN interface
items.explanation: Anti-spoofing filters are applied inbound on the external interface before routing so spoofed sources are dropped; an outbound LAN list, a VTY access-class, or an egress LAN list would not stop spoofed inbound traffic.

items.stem: An engineer must inspect traffic between a trusted LAN and an untrusted WAN, allowing return traffic automatically while denying unsolicited inbound sessions. Which feature should be configured?
items.explanation: Zone-Based Policy Firewall assigns interfaces to zones and tracks inter-zone flows so return traffic is permitted and unsolicited inbound is denied; reflexive lists are limited, and NAT and CoPP are not stateful firewalls.

items.stem: A site-to-site IPsec VPN must use a more robust key exchange with simpler negotiation and stronger certificate and rekeying support than the original version. Which version should be selected?
items.explanation: IKEv2 improves on IKEv1 with built-in NAT traversal, fewer exchanges, and stronger certificate and rekeying support; aggressive mode is less secure, and GRE without IPsec provides no encryption.

items.stem: An IPsec transform must provide both confidentiality and integrity for tunnel traffic. Which security protocol should be chosen for the transform set?
items.explanation: ESP provides confidentiality through encryption and also integrity and authentication; AH provides integrity and authentication only with no encryption, and GRE and L2TP are tunnelling protocols rather than IPsec security protocols.

items.stem: A hub-and-spoke design must let spokes build direct dynamic tunnels to each other on demand without a full mesh of statically configured tunnels. Which technology should be used?
items.explanation: DMVPN combines multipoint GRE with NHRP so spokes register with the hub and can dynamically build spoke-to-spoke tunnels; static GRE and point-to-point virtual tunnel interfaces require predefined, non-scalable tunnels.

items.stem: An enterprise wants any-to-any IPsec over an MPLS VPN with no tunnel overlay and with centralized key and policy distribution. Which technology matches this requirement?
items.explanation: GET VPN uses group keys and a key server to encrypt traffic in place without a tunnel overlay, preserving the any-to-any MPLS topology; DMVPN, static virtual tunnel interfaces, and FlexVPN create overlay tunnels.

items.stem: A security model tags each packet with a group identifier so switches and firewalls can enforce role-based policy without subnet-based access lists. Which feature provides this?
options: Cisco TrustSec with Security Group Tags
items.explanation: TrustSec assigns Security Group Tags and enforces role-based policy independent of topology; VLAN access lists, port security, and private VLANs are not identity-tag based.

items.stem: A requirement calls for hop-by-hop encryption at Layer 2 on a point-to-point link between two switches. Which technology should be used?
items.explanation: MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE) encrypts and authenticates Ethernet frames hop by hop on the link; IPsec and TLS operate at Layer 3 and above, and WPA3 secures wireless LANs.

items.stem: After DHCP snooping is enabled, an engineer wants to prevent an attacker from sending forged ARP replies on user ports. Which feature builds on the snooping binding database?
items.explanation: Dynamic ARP Inspection validates ARP packets against the DHCP snooping binding database and drops invalid replies; port security binds MACs, IP Source Guard filters assigned addresses, and BPDU guard protects spanning tree.

items.stem: A campus must prevent users from statically configuring an IP address that does not match their DHCP lease. Which feature should be enabled on access ports?
items.explanation: IP Source Guard uses the DHCP snooping binding to permit only the assigned address and optionally MAC on the port; ARP inspection protects ARP, port security limits MACs, and root guard protects spanning tree.

items.stem: A user-facing access port must immediately disable itself if any bridge protocol data units are received so a rogue switch cannot influence the topology. Which feature should be applied?
items.explanation: BPDU guard err-disables a PortFast access port when BPDUs are received; root guard stops a port from becoming root, loop guard protects blocking ports, and port security limits learned MAC addresses.

items.stem: An engineer must permit HTTPS to a specific server while denying all other traffic, and the server address changes frequently. Which design is most maintainable?
options: Inline the host address and edit the access list each time
Use a standard access list matching the destination address
Rely only on the implicit deny
Use an object group referenced in the access list and update the group when the address changes
items.explanation: Object groups centralize addresses so updates happen in one place and the access list stays stable; a standard list cannot match destination services, inlining is error prone, and the implicit deny is not a permit mechanism.

items.stem: A branch router must still authenticate administrators using a local database when the AAA server becomes unreachable. Which AAA configuration provides this?
options: Listing the local keyword after the server group for authentication fallback
Configuring RADIUS only with no fallback
Configuring TACACS+ only with no fallback
Using an enable password without AAA
items.explanation: Adding the local keyword after the server group enables fallback to the local user database when the AAA server is unreachable; server-only configurations lock out administrators, and an enable password is not AAA.

items.stem: An automation script must replace an existing REST resource with a provided representation at a known URI. Which HTTP method should be used?
items.explanation: PUT replaces the resource at a known URI and is idempotent; POST creates a resource under a collection, GET reads a resource, and HEAD retrieves headers only.

items.stem: A REST client receives an HTTP 401 response from a controller. Which condition does this status code indicate?
options: Unauthorized because authentication is required or failed
The requested resource was not found
items.explanation: HTTP 401 means the request lacks valid authentication credentials; 404 is not found, 500 is a server error, and 201 indicates a resource was created.

items.stem: A DELETE request to a REST API succeeds but the server returns no response body. Which status code is expected?
items.explanation: 204 No Content indicates a successful request with no response body, which is typical after a delete; 404 means the resource was not found, and 302 is a redirect.

items.stem: Which statement correctly describes JSON as used by REST APIs?
options: It is a text format of key and value pairs and arrays that is language independent
It is a binary protocol tied to a single vendor
It requires an external schema definition to parse
It cannot represent nested data structures
items.explanation: JSON is a lightweight, language-independent text format supporting objects, arrays, and nesting; it is not vendor-specific, does not require a schema, and fully supports nested data.

items.stem: A legacy API returns data in XML. Which statement about XML compared with JSON is accurate?
options: XML is tag based and typically more verbose, and it supports attributes and schema validation
XML is always more compact than JSON
XML cannot be validated against a schema
items.explanation: XML uses tags, is generally more verbose, and supports attributes plus schema validation with a schema definition; JSON is usually more compact, and XML is text based rather than binary-only.

items.stem: Which statement describes the role of YANG in model-driven programmability?
options: It is a physical layer encoding
It is a JSON parser used by browsers
It defines a hierarchical, tree-structured model for configuration and state data
It is a transport protocol that replaces SSH
items.explanation: YANG is a data modeling language that describes configuration and state as a tree and is consumed by NETCONF and RESTCONF; it is neither a transport protocol nor a parser.

items.stem: An engineer needs model-driven configuration over SSH that supports candidate configurations, validation, commit, and rollback. Which protocol matches these requirements?
items.explanation: NETCONF provides candidate, validate, commit, and rollback operations over SSH; RESTCONF maps YANG to HTTP methods without full transaction semantics, SNMP is legacy, and a raw CLI session is not model driven.

items.stem: Which statement about RESTCONF is correct?
options: It maps YANG-modeled data onto HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE
It uses UDP port 161 for transport
It is a Cisco-proprietary command-line interface
It replaces YANG with a vendor-specific model
items.explanation: RESTCONF exposes YANG-modeled data over HTTPS using standard HTTP verbs; it uses TCP and HTTPS rather than UDP 161, is standards based, and depends on YANG models rather than replacing them.

items.stem: A network team wants agentless, push-based configuration using YAML playbooks over SSH. Which tool fits this requirement?
items.explanation: Ansible is agentless, uses YAML playbooks and inventories, and connects over SSH; Puppet and Chef rely on agents, and a monitoring platform does not push configuration.

items.stem: A Python script must retrieve JSON from a RESTful controller over HTTP. Which standard library should make the HTTP request and decode the response?
items.explanation: The requests library performs HTTP operations and helps decode responses; paramiko handles SSH, a YAML library parses YAML, and a templating engine renders text rather than making HTTP calls.

items.stem: An engineer must programmatically retrieve device inventory from Cisco DNA Center. Which interface should the script call?
options: The DNA Center Intent API over HTTPS
items.explanation: DNA Center exposes Intent APIs (REST over HTTPS) for inventory and assurance data; SNMP and syslog are monitoring protocols, and NETCONF runs over TCP for model-driven device configuration.

items.stem: An engineer wants to run an on-box Python script on IOS-XE in response to a triggered event. Which framework enables this?
options: Embedded Event Manager with the Guest Shell
items.explanation: Embedded Event Manager can run applets and Python scripts within the IOS-XE Guest Shell when an event fires; the other options are monitoring or access protocols and do not execute on-box scripts.

items.stem: A team wants to version network automation artifacts and review proposed changes before deployment. Which practice fits this requirement?
options: Back up configurations to TFTP only
Store configurations and playbooks in Git with branches and pull requests
Keep only the current running configuration
items.explanation: Git provides distributed version control, branching, and pull-request review for automation artifacts; emailing files, keeping only the running configuration, and TFTP backups lack versioning and peer review.
